tutorial.title: Flexbox
tutorial.descriptionContent: Challenges are more difficult exercises that will test your skills.

executableContent.instructions:
Make the `#container` `<div>` a flexbox `<div>` by appropriately setting the `display` property. When finished, the game HUD panels will display horizontally.

1. Properly target the `container` div and assign an appropriate `display` property to turn it into a flexbox container.

executableContent.instructions:
We know that when applying flexbox to a container, some properties are set by default. Let's explicitly apply the appropriate `flex-direction` property such that the HUD panel stays laid out horizontally.

1. Set the `#hud` `<div>` element's `flex-direction` property so the HUD items stay in a horizontal row (left-to-right in ascending order).

Now, let's change the HUD layout back to the original setup. Appropriately set the `flex-direction` property such that the HUD elements display vertically.

1. Set the `#hud` `<div>` element's `flex-direction` property such that the HUD elements display vertically.

executableContent.instructions:
The sprite row in your game UI has too many icons, and some have started to run off the screen.

1. Appropriately assign the `flex-wrap` property on the element with ID `sprites` such that any icons overlapping the edge of the UI move to a new line.

executableContent.instructions:
Use your knowledge of Flexbox container axes to horizontally center the player sprite in the HUD bar. Select a CSS property that aligns along the main axis.

1. Appropriately assign the CSS property to horizontally center the player sprite in the `#hud` Flexbox container.

executableContent.instructions:
Use your knowledge of Flexbox container axes to position a player sprite at the bottom of the `#game-screen` container. Since the default `flex-direction` is `row`, you will need a property that aligns along the cross-axis.

1. Appropriately assign the CSS property to align the player sprite at the bottom of the `#game-screen` Flexbox container.

executableContent.instructions:
There are four HUD slots (simple `div` elements) inside a flex container. Let's make each HUD slot take up an equal amount of space so the player's UI looks balanced.

1. Assign a value of `1` to the correct property so that each HUD slot grows equally in space.

executableContent.instructions:
There are four HUD `div` elements inside a flex container. Let's make the second HUD bar (the player's health bar) larger than the rest so it stands out.

1. Make the second HUD `div` element grow `4` times larger than the rest.

executableContent.instructions:
There are four `div` elements inside the game HUD bar. Let’s make the second and last HUD slots larger than the rest (think: a bigger Health bar and Score panel).

1. Add the correct `display` property and value for `.hud` to make it a `flex` container.
2. Make the second and last `div` element grow `4` times the space of the rest.
